content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Warner Robins

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a bachelor's degree plus three years of project-management experience, or a high school diploma plus five years of experience. Verify your education and hours logged managing projects. Professionals in Aerospace & Defense, Government, and Defense Contracting roles at major employers often meet these thresholds early in their careers.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP course delivered nationwide. Attend scheduled sessions from your Warner Robins location on your own schedule. Our active certified practitioners cover all five process groups and ten knowledge areas required by PMI, with real-world examples relevant to your industry.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: Create your PMI account and formally apply for PMP candidacy through the PMI website. Upload proof of education and project experience hours. Pay the exam fee directly to PMI. Allow time for application review before scheduling your exam appointment.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Take the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and final review sessions—to build confidence. Schedule your exam at a Pearson VUE testing center. Sit for the 180-question, computer-based exam that assesses your mastery of project-management domains and processes.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After certification, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) every three years to renew your PMP. Pursue education, volunteer roles, or project-delivery experience aligned with PMI's continuing-learning standards. Renewal keeps your credential active and your project-management skills current in your local market.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI sets four eligibility paths based on education: a secondary diploma (high school or equivalent) requires 60 months of project leadership experience; an associate's degree requires 48 months; a bachelor's degree requires 36 months; and a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI Global Accreditation Center (GAC)-accredited program requires just 24 months. Every path also requires 35 hours of project management education — our course satisfies this requirement in full.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.
